_comment: COORD-624: the payload's OWN declaration of what each of its paths is for.
Concord installs into a PARENT WORKSPACE and lives as a SIBLING of the
product repositories it governs:
project-workspace/
|-- coord/        <- Concord control plane   (class: workspace)
|-- .claude/      <- agent integration        (class: workspace)
|-- AGENTS.md
|-- repo-one/     <- independent product Git repository (NOT ours)
|-- repo-two/     <- independent product Git repository (NOT ours)
`-- repo-three/   <- independent product Git repository (NOT ours)
The install engine derives the payload it may emit FROM THIS FILE. It is a
positive declaration of surfaces, never a post-hoc cleanup/delete list:
the reviewed install plan is built only from the selected classes, so a
product-sample path can never appear as an operation in the first place.
Anti-drift teeth (all fail closed, all in buildInstallPlan):
1. TOTALITY  - every file in the payload must match at least one declared
surface path prefix. Add a new top-level directory to the template and
the installer REFUSES until it is classified here.
2. CLASS MAPPING - every declared class must be mapped by every mode.
Invent a new class and every install refuses until the modes name it.
3. CONFIG CROSS-CHECK - every repo path declared in the payload's own
coord/project.config.js `repos` map must classify as product-sample.
Mis-filing sample product scaffolding as governance is refused.
Classification is LONGEST-PREFIX-WINS, so a more specific path overrides a
broader one. Paths are payload-relative and use the payload's SOURCE names
(the npm channel ships the workspace ignore policy as pack-safe `gitignore`;
both names are declared).

governance-engine.description: The vendored Concord control plane: engine scripts, board, schemas, product docs, workflow packs.

agent-integration.description: Workspace-level agent integration: slash commands, skills, MCP settings and the per-provider workspace guides.

workspace-docs.description: Adopter-facing workspace documentation and project meta files.

workspace-bootstrap.description: Workspace recovery/upgrade bootstrap, runtime ignore policy and cut provenance stamp. Transactional installers are distribution artifacts and are not installed into the workspace payload.

retired-donor-entrypoints.description: Retired compatibility shims retained only so source-checkout bookmarks fail with write-free recovery guidance. No install mode may emit them, and the release builder strips them.

workspace-config.description: The WORKSPACE-mode variant of the project-owned config seam. It is emitted AS coord/project.config.js and starts with an empty repos map, because in the sibling model the adopter's repositories are theirs to map with `concord onboard`. Declared as its own class so it and the sample-product variant can never both be selected.

sample-product.description: TEMPLATE PRODUCT SCAFFOLDING. A demonstration two-repo product layout plus the bundled demo workspace, and the project.config.js that maps them. INSTALLATION NEVER EMITS ANY OF IT — see non_installable_classes.

_non_installable_rationale: Installation installs GOVERNANCE ONLY and never creates or modifies product
repositories. A mode that wrote product code during installation would not be
an exception to that rule with a friendly name — it would mean the rule is
false. So `product-sample` is reachable by NO install mode, and the installer
refuses any mode that tries to select it.
Creating the sample/demo project is therefore a separate, explicitly consented
POST-INSTALL operation, not an install mode. Until that operation ships,
greenfield demo creation is unavailable — a deliberate, stated gap rather than
a product-writing install path kept alive to hide it.
The paths stay declared here because the TOTALITY check requires every payload
path to be classified: they must be named to be excluded, and naming them is
what makes their exclusion derived rather than hardcoded.
The donor-only class holds retired compatibility entry points. It is also
reachable by no install mode: keeping a refusal shim for old source-checkout
bookmarks must never turn it back into a distributed installation channel.

workspace.description: THE — and only — installation model: overlay the governance control plane onto a parent workspace whose product repositories are independent sibling Git repositories. Emits no product scaffolding, and never creates or modifies a product repository.
